   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  April 30, 2025
 To:  Audit and Finance Committee
 From:  Jeff S. Muir, Director of Finance
  Tatiana Szerwinski, Assistant Director of Finance
  Sivan Levin, Financial Planning & Research Analyst
 Subject:  Business Tax Consultant Services per Recommendation from the
  Blue Ribbon Committee
 Attachments:  None.

At the March 18, 2024 City Council Study Session, City Treasurer, Howard Fisher,
and Finance Director, Jeff Muir, presented the report and recommendations by the
Blue Ribbon Committee on long-term strategic financial planning. City Council
provided staff direction to proceed with a business tax study, one of the four major
revenue sources of the City.
The purpose for the study is to update and modernize the City’s Business Tax
provisions to support economic growth and job creation and to ensure a flexible,
forward-looking, and equitable business tax program. The potential changes are
intended to:
•  Attract, retain, and encourage expansion of businesses within the City,
•  Create a fair, equitable and simple business tax system,
•  Support small businesses and microenterprises,
•  Address and appropriately tax emerging business models,
•  Ensure the taxing scheme is competitive with neighboring jurisdictions with
  similar characteristics,
•  Minimize administration and compliance costs for the City and taxpayers,
•  Protect the City’s fiscal position, and
•  Be structured so that business oversight and compliance is not overly
  burdensome for City staff or affected businesses, and so that oversight and
  compliance is consistent with other City laws, taxes, and reporting procedures.
 City staff is working on a Request for Proposal (RFP) for a business tax consultant
to provide professional services to assist the City in the following:
•  Conduct an initial study analyzing the City’s current business tax program (as
  currently defined in Title 3, Article 2 of the Beverly Hills Municipal Code) in the
  context of the City’s goals for the program. The study would include:
  (a) A benchmarking analysis of surrounding and similarly situated
  municipalities and an overview of trends and opportunities in this area
  based on current academic research and industry best practices;
  (b) A review identifying where the City could make municipal code language
  updates that would help to reach its goals.
•  Based on initial study results, and with additional direction from City
  leadership, develop business taxation and financial models and provide tax
  proposals and recommendations for consideration.
•  Assist with conducting community and business outreach throughout the
  process.
•  Assist in drafting a proposed ordinance.
•  Provide recommendations for and assist in implementation and development
  of metrics and benchmarks for monitoring the success of the tax reform after
  implementation.
•  Assist with internal and external communication, including presence at City
  Council meetings when appropriate.
The RFP is requesting a single consultant that will be able to provide all of the
requested services. However, staff will consider awarding different components
of the work to different consultants should that be in the best interest of the City.
Staff is working with the City Attorney’s office to finalize the RFP and will release
it through PlanetBids, the City’s online portal for bid solicitation. Upon review, staff
will bring back its recommendation to the Audit and Finance Committee and then
look to finalize the contract award by the end of the fiscal year/early next fiscal
year.
